headline: Eid-e-Miladunnabi to be observed on August 26 in Bangladesh
summary: The National Moon Sighting Committee has confirmed the date after the moon of Rabiul Awal was not sighted on Thursday.
details: The National Moon Sighting Committee has announced that Eid-e-Miladunnabi (PBUH) will be celebrated across Bangladesh on Wednesday, August 26.
The decision was made during a meeting chaired by Religious Affairs Ministry Secretary Munshi Alauddin Al Azad at the Baitul Mukarram conference room on Thursday evening.

The committee reviewed data from all district administrations, the Islamic Foundation's head and regional offices, the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, and SPARRSO to confirm that the moon of Rabiul Awal was not sighted on Thursday.
As a result, the month of Safar will complete 30 days on Friday, August 14, and the holy month of Rabiul Awal 1448 Hijri will begin on Saturday, August 15.
Eid-e-Miladunnabi marks the birth and passing of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), who is revered as the final messenger of Islam and the bringer of a message of peace and monotheism.
Devout Muslims will observe the day through Quran recitation, prayers, charity, and voluntary fasts.

headline_marked: Energy crisis deepens as [[load shedding reaches Dhaka]] and fuel shortages hit
headline: Energy crisis deepens as load shedding reaches Dhaka and fuel shortages hit
summary: Power outages and gas shortages are causing widespread disruption, with drivers waiting in long queues and protesters blocking highways in Jamalpur.
details: Bangladesh is facing a deepening energy crisis characterized by widespread load shedding and severe gas shortages, affecting both the capital city of Dhaka and other districts.
In Dhaka, power outages are now frequent, disrupting daily life and businesses as the national grid struggles to meet demand.
CNG-powered vehicles are facing extreme difficulties, with drivers spending hours in long queues for gas, some even falling asleep in their vehicles while waiting.
The situation has escalated into protests, with drivers in Jamalpur blocking major highways to demand a steady supply of gas.
Experts and reports suggest that planning failures in the energy sector have contributed significantly to the current crisis.
The energy shortage is impacting multiple sectors, from transportation and fuel stations to residential power supply.
caption:
From long gas queues to highway blockades, Bangladesh's energy crisis is hitting hard.

Bangladesh is facing a deepening energy crisis characterized by widespread load shedding and severe gas shortages, affecting both the capital city of Dhaka and other districts.

In Dhaka, power outages are now frequent, disrupting daily life and businesses as the national grid struggles to meet demand.

CNG-powered vehicles are facing extreme difficulties, with drivers spending hours in long queues for gas, some even falling asleep in their vehicles while waiting.

The situation has escalated into protests, with drivers in Jamalpur blocking major highways to demand a steady supply of gas.

Experts and reports suggest that planning failures in the energy sector have contributed significantly to the current crisis.

The energy shortage is impacting multiple sectors, from transportation and fuel stations to residential power supply.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star
